scientific_rationale: Women are underrepresented in cardiovascular clinical trials. The Framingham Risk Score was derived primarily from male cohorts. This case demonstrates multi-modal AI-assisted preventive health monitoring for a demographic with distinct risk profiles and symptom presentations.

lipid_panel.ldl_status: borderline — below statin threshold but above optimal

family_history.risk_multiplier: bilateral first-degree history elevates risk above Framingham estimate

medications.name: lisinopril
medications.notes: minimum effective dose; cardioprotective beyond BP lowering

rationale.APOE: Apolipoprotein E — lipid transport; e4 allele elevates LDL and dementia risk
rationale.LDLR: LDL receptor — familial hypercholesterolemia spectrum; premature MI in father
rationale.ACE: Angiotensin-converting enzyme — current lisinopril target; pharmacogenomics
rationale.PCSK9: Proprotein convertase — emerging therapeutic target for LDL reduction
rationale.LPA: Lipoprotein(a) — independent CVD risk factor; not captured by standard lipid panel
rationale.9p21: Chromosome 9p21 locus — strongest genetic risk locus for coronary artery disease

risk_scores.reynolds_rationale: Reynolds Risk Score was specifically validated in women and incorporates hsCRP and family history — both elevated in this patient. Use Reynolds as primary estimate.

genetic_screening.interpretation: No pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants detected in 11 genes analyzed. Does not eliminate polygenic or environmental cardiovascular risk. Diagnostic testing recommended given bilateral first-degree family history.

familial_hypercholesterolemia.clinical_pivot: Monogenic FH effectively ruled out. LDL elevation (118 mg/dL) and bilateral family history are more likely polygenic and environmental in origin. Risk mechanism shifts from single-variant to aggregate polygenic burden.

lynch_syndrome.caveat: PMS2 exons 11-15 excluded due to pseudogene overlap with PMS2CL

APOE.rationale: APOE e4 allele is the strongest common genetic risk factor for late-onset cardiovascular disease and Alzheimer's disease. Particularly relevant post-menopause at age 67. Not included in population screening panels — requires separate clinical order.
APOE.recommendation: Discuss APOE genotyping with physician. Result would inform both cardiovascular and cognitive health monitoring strategy.

LPA.rationale: Lipoprotein(a) is genetically determined, does not respond to lifestyle modification or standard lipid-lowering therapy, and is an independent CVD risk factor not captured by standard lipid panels. Elevated Lp(a) would reclassify this patient to higher risk.
LPA.recommendation: Order serum Lp(a) blood test. Measure once — it does not meaningfully change over time. If elevated (>50 mg/dL or >125 nmol/L), risk reclassification and more aggressive LDL targets are warranted.

coronary_artery_calcium.rationale: CAC score is the most powerful reclassifier for intermediate-risk patients like PAT003. CAC=0 would reclassify to low risk and likely defer statin initiation; CAC>100 would accelerate treatment.
coronary_artery_calcium.recommendation: Discuss CAC scoring at next cardiology visit. Low radiation, one-time test, highly informative for this risk profile.

polygenic_risk_score_cvd.rationale: Tier 1 screens report only high-impact single variants. Aggregate polygenic burden from thousands of small-effect common variants — which likely explains PAT003's family history — is not captured by this test.
polygenic_risk_score_cvd.recommendation: CVD polygenic risk score (PRS) is not yet standard of care but increasingly available through research programs. Would quantify inherited polygenic burden independently of single-gene findings.

9p21_locus.rationale: Chromosome 9p21 is the strongest GWAS-identified locus for coronary artery disease and is not included in clinical panels.
9p21_locus.recommendation: Captured by CVD PRS if ordered. Not actionable as a standalone test currently.

clinical_reinterpretation.reynolds_rationale: Negative FH screen does not lower the Reynolds Risk Score (14.2%). Bilateral family history remains a risk factor regardless of FH gene status — it may reflect shared polygenic burden, shared environment, or both.
clinical_reinterpretation.statin_decision_impact: More nuanced post-screen. Without FH, borderline LDL (118 mg/dL) at intermediate Reynolds risk is not an automatic statin indication for women. ACC/AHA guidelines suggest CAC scoring as the preferred next step for reclassification in this scenario.
priority_action_sequence: 1. Order serum Lp(a) — one-time test, low cost, high impact on risk classification
2. Discuss APOE genotyping — informs both CVD and cognitive monitoring
3. Consider CAC scoring — best reclassification tool available for intermediate risk
4. Reassess statin decision after Lp(a) and CAC results are known

monitoring_plan.lpa_test: once — does not change with lifestyle
monitoring_plan.calcium_score_cac: consider at next cardiology visit — CAC=0 would reclassify to low risk
